You have asked me to explain the reasons why we have requested that the Board of Commissioners of Treutlen County adopt a resolution providing for the assessment and collection of an ad valorem tax, if required, to pay debt service on the Series 2010 Bonds.

I. Background and authority for issuance of school debt

On September 18, 2007, the voters of Treutlen County voted in favor of the issuance of general obligation debt in the principal amount not to exceed $7,920,000 for various capital outlay projects, including a new school for students in K-12, for the Treutlen County School District. The voters also voted in favor of reimposing a one percent sales and use tax for educational purposes (“ESPLOST”) for a period of time not to exceed 20 consecutive calendar quarters.

The general obligation debt approved by the voters was validated by order of the Superior Court of Treutlen County on January 31, 2008, Civil Action No. 08-CI-0005. The order of the Court states as follows:

IT IS FURTHER DETERMINED, ORDERED AND ADJUDGED that the Bonds shall be and the same hereby are in each and every respect confirmed and validated, and that the School District is authorized and empowered to issue and deliver the Bonds in conformity with the law in such cases made and provided for the purposes set forth in the petition of the District Attorney and the answer of the School District, and prior to the issuance of the Bonds, the Board of Education is authorized to take and did take all steps lawfully required to impose, levy and collect a one percent sales and use tax for educational purposes and will recommend to the Board of Commissioners of Treutlen County that said Board assess and collect a continuing direct annual tax on all the taxable property

‘ November 29, 2010 Page 2 of 3 located within the boundaries of the School District sufficient in an amount to pay the principal of and interest on the Bonds as the same shall mature and become due to the extent the proceeds of the sales and use tax for educational purposes received by the School District are not sufficient for that purpose; and prior to the issuance of the Bonds, the Board of Commissioners of Treutlen County is authorized to take and will take all necessary actions to assess and collect said tax, and, when the Bonds shall be so issued and delivered, the Bonds shall be valid and binding general obligations of the School District in accordance with the terms and provisions thereof, all the terms and provisions of which Bonds are hereby in each and every respect confirmed and validated. (Emphasis Added)

Levy of taxes to pay bonds; ...Any county, municipality, or other political subdivision of this state shall at or before the time of incurring bonded indebtedness provide for the assessment and collection of an annual tax sufficient in amount to pay the principal and interest of said debt within 30 years from the incurring of such bonded indebtedness...

This Constitutional provision must be complied with before debt is incurred. See Woodall v. Town of Adel, 122. Ga. 301 (1905). No plan for otherwise raising funds can be lawfully substituted. See Wilkins v. Waynesboro, 116 Ga. 259 (1902).

In addition to the validation order, the Superior Court of Treutlen County on November 19, 2010, Civil Action No. 10-C]-0258, declared that the Treutlen County School District has the authority to issue the authorized general obligation debt in the form of “Qualified School Construction Bonds”, as created by Congress in the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009. The issuance of the general obligation bonds as Qualified School Construction Bonds will enable the School District to apply for “Subsidy Credits” from the United States Treasury where the School District will be reimbursed for 100% of the interest costs on the bonds.

Il. Action by the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners

Although the resolution which we have submitted to the Board of Commissioners provides for the assessment and collection of an annual tax in an amount sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the debt, reference is made to other sources which are expected to be available for such purpose, i.e., ESPLOST and Subsidy Credits from the U.S. Treasury. As long as the ESPLOST is continued by the voters of Treutlen County in the future and the Subsidy Credits are sent to the School District, it is not anticipated that a tax will need to be levied to pay principal of and interest on the Series 2010 Bonds. However, in order to comply with Georgia law, the School District must provide for the assessment and collection of such tax. This is consistent with established Georgia case law. See Sewell v. City of Tallapoosa, 145 Ga. 19 (7) (1916).
